“Thud?”

“Huh?”

?

“…Huh? What are you doing here, Tohsaka?”

“What does it look like? I went home to collect my things. I'll be living here from today, so naturally I needed them.”

“…Huh? What are you here for, Tohsaka?”
“I just went to go get my stuff from my house. It’s natural, since I’ll be living here from now on.”

“That's what cooperating means. …What exactly did you think we were discussing earlier?”

I am too stunned to speak.

I have to object. If I don't say something, this will turn into a disaster—but my mind refuses to work.

Something. I have to say something back, or something terrible is going to happen, but my head will not function.

“Oh, why don’t you prepare a room for her as well? Your Servant takes up space unlike my Archer, so you should give her a place to sleep. Well, if just one bed is no problem for you then I wouldn’t mind.”
Wait… that… that means sleeping in the same bed, right?!

Saber makes a difficult face.

“That presents a problem, Shirou. A Servant exists to protect her Master. You require the greatest protection while asleep. I cannot guard you unless we share a room.”

“That puts me in an even worse position! What are the two of you thinking? Are you really women!?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“That is not good, Shirou. Servants are to protect their Masters. The hours of sleep are the most crucial time for protecting you, so I cannot protect you unless I am in the same room.”
“I’m in more trouble even if you say that! What are you thinking, are you two really girls!?”

“I see. I can watch myself if you don't like it. Do you mind, Shirou?”

Tohsaka says it with perfect composure, oblivious to what she is doing to me.

…You were absolutely right, Issei.

There is something terrifyingly bewitching about Rin Tohsaka.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see. I’ll be careful if you don’t like that, but don’t you like it?”
Tohsaka says so plainly, without realizing what I’m feeling.
…Geez, it’s just like you said, Issei.
I think Tohsaka Rin is a real devil.

“Rin, do not end the discussion. We have yet to decide the matter of Shirou's room and mine.”

“Really? Then I’ll do that.”
“Rin, please do not end the conversation. We have not come up with a solution to the matter of the room for Shirou and I.”

“Oh, right. But with Shirou acting like this, sharing a room seems impossible. Treating a Servant as human does no good, but he says he doesn't want it, so why not give up?”

“That is not what he said. Shirou said it would present a problem. He did not say he was unwilling.”

“There you have it. What do you say to that distinction, Shirou?”

“Oh, of course, of course. But it’ll be hard to stay in the same room with Shirou acting like that. There’s no point in treating a Servant like a human, but why don’t you give up since Shirou doesn’t want it?”
“That is incorrect. Shirou only said it would trouble him, and he did not say he did not want it.”
“Well then. What do you say, Shirou?”

Saber says it as though it were self-evident.

Only now does the truth strike me.

I have been given a sword far too great for my hand.

Saber says this as if it’s just something natural.
That makes me realize even more,
that I have been given a sword I do not deserve.

pages.en:
Unable to recover her magical energy, she must fight while always guarding the dwindling amount that remains.

Forced to battle in shackles, deprived of her freedom—

That was what left her body drenched in red blood.
pages.mirrorMoon:
In her condition, unable to replenish magical energy, she always has to think about her remaining magical energy.
The result of a battle with such a burden was…
…That image of her covered in blood.

“It is not as though I have never known defeat.

“It is because I failed to achieve victory that I now stand here as your Servant. I am accustomed to being wounded. There is no reason for you to reproach yourself.”

“It is not as if I suffered no defeat.
I am your Servant now because I did not fully win. I am used to taking wounds, so it is not something you should mourn over.”

“Accustomed to it…? Even injuries that nearly kill you?”

“Yes. To take up a sword is to accept injury. The same is true of you, is it not? There is no reason I alone should remain unhurt.”

“Used to…? Even wounds close to fatal?”
“Yes. To wield a sword means to take injury as well. That should be the same for you too. There is no reason for just me to avoid harm.”

…Rin’s words are certainly correct. There is no need to treat Servants as humans. We are a tool to protect our Master. You must understand that.”
